title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This integrated playbook documents Redwood Inference’s recommended workflows for onboarding models into the Eval Harness, creating and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, authoring quantization profiles, and running an operational regression triage process. The goal is reproducible, auditable quality control that keeps model-serving SLOs and customer-facing quality metrics within acceptable bounds while enabling rapid iteration.

Scope:
- Applies to all open and internal model variants onboarded to Redwood-hosted and dedicated inference runtimes.
- Covers: Eval Harness configuration, prompt set lifecycle, benchmark selection, quantization profiling, and regression triage.
- Excludes low-risk research prototypes (see threshold criteria below).

Why this matters:
- Prevents silent quality regressions when changing model checkpoints, quantization levels, or prompt/template updates.
- Provides a common language and tooling for ML engineers, applied ML, and platform SREs to triage and remediate issues quickly.

Owner & Roles:
- Playbook owner: Applied ML (Asha Patel) — contact: asha.patel@redwood.ai
- Eval Harness maintainers: Applied ML / Eval Platform (reviewers listed)
- Onboarding owner: Model Onboarding team (product/engineering collaboration)
- Incident owner for regressions: Model Reliability (eng-sre escalation on-call)

Key Services and Dashboards:
- Eval Harness service: eval-harness.redwood.internal (primary job to run automated suites)
- PromptSet Catalog: prompt-sets.redwood.internal (registry and versioning)
- Quantization Profiler: qprof.redwood.internal (generates candidate profiles and performance estimates)
- Regression Triage dashboard: grafana/dashboard/evals-regression (aggregated alerts, regressions by prompt-set)

SLOs & Alerting Thresholds (applies to production deployments):
- Quality pass rate: >= 95% on core prompt set (see Core Prompt Set below)
- Hallucination rate: <= 1% on factual QA benchmarks
- Latency impact from quantization: p95 latency increase <= 10% relative to baseline float32
- Automated regression alert: >= 5 percentage point drop in pass rate on any monitored prompt set OR any single-test failure in high-severity prompt lists
- Manual review trigger: any customer-reported semantic regression OR automatic alert that persists for > 1 hour

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1. Pre-onboard validation
   - Confirm model artifacts: architecture, tokenizer, config, and expected seq-length.
   - Run unit smoke tests locally (unit test list included in Eval Harness repo).
2. Eval Harness baseline run
   - Add a new model entry in eval-harness with model_id and version tags.
   - Execute full baseline suite: core prompt set, safety checks, latency/throughput microbenchmarks.
   - Required artifact: baseline report (JSON) saved to S3 path: s3://eval-results/{model_id}/{version}/baseline.json
3. Prompt set onboarding
   - Create a PromptSet package in the PromptSet Catalog. Use the naming convention: ps-{domain}-{intended-use}-{YYYYMMDD}.
   - For each prompt, include: canonical input, expected outputs (gold labels or heuristics), severity tag (core/high/low), and evaluation metric (accuracy/ROUGE/F1/custom).
4. Quantization profiling
   - Run qprof to generate candidate 8-bit and 4-bit profiles. Record expected memory reduction and estimated perf.
   - Verify functional parity on a quantization verification prompt set (small subset targeted at numeric stability and tokenization edge cases).
5. Canary rollout
   - Canary size: 1-5% traffic (depending on customer tier). Monitor evaluation metrics and latency for 48 hours.
   - If automated metrics pass and no customer incidents, proceed to staged rollout.

Prompt sets and benchmark guidelines:
- Core Prompt Set (required for all production models):
  - ~300 examples covering high-frequency intents and edge cases.
  - Balanced across languages and token lengths representative of production traffic.
  - Must include: factual QA, instruction-following, code generation smoke tests, and safety examples.
- Severity tagging: each prompt must be tagged core/high/medium/low. Alerts only raised automatically for core and high prompts.
- Versioning: Prompt sets are immutable once published. Create new versions with changelog and migration notes.
- Quality metrics: specify metric per prompt (e.g., exact-match, semantic-similarity threshold, BLEURT/RUBERT) and threshold values.

Benchmark selection and periodicity:
- Full suite: run nightly against all production model variants. Includes Core Prompt Set, Safety Set, and Latency/Throughput microbenchmarks.
- Quick smoke: run on every model push (CI) - contains 50 representative prompts to detect major regressions.
- Release gating: require two consecutive nightly full-suite passes for major version promotion.

Quantization profile best practices:
- Profiles capture: quantization method (PTQ/QAT), bit-width, per-channel vs per-tensor, calibration dataset, and fallback rules.
- Recommended default profiles:
  - q8-perchannel-ptq: target for most production workloads with <5% quality delta on Core Prompt Set.
  - q4-dynamic: use only for non-critical workloads where memory is the gating factor; require explicit product approval.
- Calibration dataset: use 10k representative in-domain examples with coverage across token lengths. Document dataset id in profile metadata.
- Safety checks: run safety-related prompts post-quantization; if hallucination rate increases by >0.5 percentage points, block rollout.

Regression triage playbook (operational runbook):
1. Detect
   - Automated alert triggers in Grafana (see thresholds above) or via customer report.
2. Triage (0-15 minutes)
   - Assign incident lead (Model Reliability). Pull latest Eval Harness reports for the model and version.
   - Identify whether regression is: prompt-specific, metric-wide, or infrastructure-related (e.g., kernel change, batching issue).
3. Isolate (15-60 minutes)
   - Re-run failing prompt(s) against: current prod variant, prior-good variant, and local debug build.
   - If failures only on quantized variant, tag as quantization-regression and escalate to Quantization owners.
4. Remediate (1-8 hours)
   - Common fixes: revert recent model rollouts, adjust prompt templates, update quantization profile with more calibration data, or apply a temporary routing policy (fallback to float32).
   - For model-level regressions, open an ADR if root cause is design change; otherwise patch and redeploy.
5. Close and document (within 24 hours)
   - Publish post-incident summary to confluence under applied-ml-and-evals/postmortems and mark the fix in the model’s onboarding record.

Artifacts and required metadata for every run:
- baseline.json (S3) - pass/fail per prompt, per-metric deltas, perf counters
- qprof-report.txt (S3) - quantization estimates and observed deltas
- promptset-version.txt - catalog id and version of each prompt set used
- run-id and kubernetes/job id for reproducibility

Example commands and snippets:
- Run quick smoke locally: 
  ./eval-harness/run.sh --model-id model-bert-001 --suite smoke --out s3://eval-results/model-bert-001/$(date +%F)/smoke.json
- Generate quantization profile:
  qprof profile --model model-bert-001 --calib-dataset s3://datasets/calib-10k --out s3://qprof/model-bert-001/q8-profile.json

Quality gates checklist (pre-rollout):
- Nightly full-suite: pass for 2 consecutive runs.
- Latency impact within thresholds (p95 <= baseline * 1.10).
- No safety regressions flagged by the safety suite.
- Quantization profile verified on verification prompt set if used.

Known limitations & escalation notes:
- Small prompt sets may miss low-frequency regressions; increase coverage for high-risk customers.
- Certain hallucination classes are metric-hard to detect; rely on human-in-loop evaluation for major public-facing features.

Appendix: quick reference tables

Core rollout thresholds:
- Quality pass rate: >= 95%
- Auto-alert delta: >= 5 percentage points drop
- Canary duration: 48 hours

Quantization profiles summary (example entries):
- q8-perchannel-ptq | avg mem reduction: 3.8x | expected p95 latency delta: -5% to +8% | recommended: general production
- q4-dynamic | avg mem reduction: 8x | expected p95 latency delta: -10% to +35% | recommended: memory-constrained, risk-reviewed
